subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Locomotor Combinations, Pathways, and Dynamic Space
title: Performance task build: changing direction and pathway at speed
focus: changing direction and pathway at speed
essentialQuestion: How do I combine travel patterns and read space that keeps changing?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Lower your body slightly before cutting.
Make the change sharp and definite.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Rounded turns that give away the intention. Fix: use cone gates that force a sharp angle.
keyPoints: Lower your body slightly before cutting.
Make the change sharp and definite.
privacySafeScenario: Perform a travel sequence through a changing space and explain how you found and used open space.
studentTask: The learner practises changing direction and pathway at speed at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with changing direction and pathway at speed and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about changing direction and pathway at speed at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for changing direction and pathway at speed.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Each locomotor pattern has an equivalent the learner can perform: arm-driven or wheelchair propulsion for travel, seated marching or stepping in place for hop and gallop, and rhythm tapping for skip. Distance, height, and repetition are always adjustable and never compared between learners.
extensionChallenge: Apply changing direction and pathway at speed under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises changing direction and pathway at speed. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
